name: wps_pwd_auth_fail
prose: Event handler for a WPS "password authentication failed" event on a BSS (wps_hostapd.c:738-787; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on every path (743, 756, 786), so the return value is always 0 here. It does nothing if the failure is not an enrollee failure, no AP PIN is configured or WPS is not running (742-743). Otherwise it increments the total and the consecutive failure counters (750-751) and returns if fewer than 3 failures have been counted in total (755-756). From the third failure it sets ap_setup_locked in the WPS state and updates the registrar's information elements (759-761). If the configuration does not itself lock AP setup: with 10 or more consecutive failures it cancels the automatic AP PIN re-enable timeout (indefinite lock) (763-769); with fewer it sets the lockout time to 60 seconds the first time, doubles it each third failure while it is under a year, cancels any pending re-enable timeout and registers a new timeout of that length for hostapd_wps_reenable_ap_pin (771-783).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: the code has no return statement after the third-failure path, so it does not always return 0 - wrong: wps_hostapd.c:786 is `return 0;` after the whole third-failure handling and every other exit is also `return 0`. Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: dpp_controller_rx_gas_comeback_req
prose: Handles a GAS comeback request received over TCP by the DPP controller (dpp_tcp.c:1492-1530; slice cut the head); it returns -1 on failure and otherwise the result of the send helper. It returns -1 if the message is empty, if there is no auth, if neither a control connection nor a configurator exists, if the authentication or reconfiguration was not successful, if no GAS comeback is in progress (1499-1510), or if the dialog token differs from the stored one (1512-1516). If no configuration response is ready yet it returns dpp_tcp_send_comeback_delay (1519-1523). Otherwise it takes ownership of auth->conf_resp_tcp by moving the pointer into a local and setting auth->conf_resp_tcp to NULL, then returns dpp_tcp_send_gas_resp(conn, WLAN_PA_GAS_COMEBACK_RESP, resp) (1527-1529); that helper frees the buffer in all cases, including when it fails to allocate the outgoing message and returns -1 (dpp_tcp.c:1346-1357, 1370), so the response buffer is consumed on this path even on failure.
note: [R:right] reviewer: on wpabuf allocation failure it sets auth->conf_resp_tcp to NULL and frees that buffer, so it is not side-effect-free - right (1528 clears the pointer before the call; dpp_tcp_send_gas_resp frees resp when its allocation fails, 1353-1356). Slice cut the head; function read in full, plus dpp_tcp_send_gas_resp.

name: dpp_controller_rx
prose: Socket read callback of the DPP controller TCP connection (dpp_tcp.c:1739-1856; the packet name dpp_controller_rx_msg does not exist). It first reads the 4-byte message length: a read error or end of stream removes the connection (dpp_connection_remove) and returns; a partial length returns to wait for more; a length above 65535 removes the connection; otherwise it frees any old buffer and allocates a message buffer of that length (1748-1787). If there is no buffer it removes the connection and returns (1789-1794). It reads into the buffer's tailroom; a read error or end of stream removes the connection and returns (1799-1809); it appends the received bytes and, while the buffer still has tailroom, returns to wait (1811-1818). When the message is complete it resets msg_len_octets to 0, removes the connection if the message is empty, and otherwise dispatches on the first byte: vendor specific to dpp_controller_rx_action, GAS initial request to dpp_controller_rx_gas_req, GAS initial or comeback response to dpp_rx_gas_resp and GAS comeback request to dpp_controller_rx_gas_comeback_req, each followed by removal of the connection if the handler returns a negative value; an unknown type only logs (1820-1855). It returns nothing.
note: [R:n/a] still-rejected only for the wrong name; the real function is dpp_controller_rx (dpp_tcp.c:1739-1856), fixed under that name, read in full; the dispatched handlers not read.

name: is_punct_bitmap_valid
prose: Checks that a channel puncturing bitmap is valid for a bandwidth (hw_features_common.c:987-1035; slice cut the head); it returns true for a valid bitmap and false otherwise, and it only reads its arguments and constant tables. A zero punct_bitmap returns true (993-994). Otherwise it inverts the bitmap, masks it to the width of the bandwidth (4 bits for 80, 8 bits for 160, 16 bits for 320 MHz) and selects the matching table of valid patterns; any other bw returns false (996-1019). It returns false if the resulting active-channel bitmap is zero, or if the bit for the primary channel (pri_ch_bit_pos) is not set in it (1021-1027), and otherwise returns true only if the active bitmap equals one of the entries of the table for that bandwidth (1029-1034). pri_ch_bit_pos is used as a shift count without a range check.
note: [R:n/a] the reviewer's remark compared the formal contract with the prose; the contract field is left empty here since the function reads constant global tables (punct_bitmap_80/160/320). Slice cut the head; function read in full (987-1035).

name: nan_de_next_multicast
prose: Computes when the next multicast NAN service discovery frame should be sent for a service (nan_de.c:423-464; slice cut the head); it returns -1 if no multicast frame is wanted, 0 if one is due now, and otherwise the time to wait in milliseconds. It returns -1 for a publish service that is not unsolicited and for a subscribe service that is not active (429-432). If no multicast frame has been sent yet (last_multicast not initialised) it returns 0 (434-435); this test comes before the publish checks that return -1 for a TTL of 0 or for a pause that has an end time set (437-442), so those checks apply only after a first multicast has been sent. It then adds the announcement period (publish) or query period (subscribe), 100 ms if 0, to last_multicast (444-450). For a publish service it returns 0 if no transmit wait is pending and the next time is already in the past, otherwise it continues with next_publish_state (452-457). It returns 0 if the computed time is before now, otherwise the difference in milliseconds (459-463).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the publish ttl/pause -1 checks occur after the uninitialised last_multicast returns 0 - right (434-435 before 437-442). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: rijndaelKeySetupEnc
prose: Expands an AES cipher key into the encryption round-key schedule (aes-internal.c:779-845; the packet name is an excerpt, the function is rijndaelKeySetupEnc); it returns the number of rounds or -1. It first reads the first 16 key bytes into rk[0..3] (784-787). For keyBits 128 it writes 40 more words with ten rounds of the key schedule and returns 10 (789-799). For other values it reads 8 more key bytes into rk[4..5] and, for 192, runs the 192-bit schedule and returns 12 from inside the loop (802-818). For any value other than 128 and 192 it also reads 8 more key bytes into rk[6..7], and for 256 runs the 256-bit schedule and returns 14 from inside the loop (821-841). For every other keyBits value it returns -1 (844); in that case it has already read 32 key bytes and written rk[0..7]. The caller must provide a writable rk with room for the schedule (44, 52 or 60 words) and a key of 16, 24 or 32 bytes, and a key shorter than 32 bytes is also over-read when keyBits is not 128 or 192.
note: [R:right] reviewer: the formal contract omits the prose preconditions and the rk write side effects; "requires \true" is weaker - right, so the contract field is left empty (pointer parameters). Function read in full (779-845); TE4xx and GETU32 macros not read.

name: check_ocsp_resp
prose: Checks the OCSP response attached to a TLS connection for the peer certificate cert (tls_openssl_ocsp.c, check_ocsp_resp at 480-840; the packet name check_ocsp does not exist, and the slice 506-763 is inside it); it returns an enum ocsp_result: OCSP_GOOD, OCSP_REVOKED, OCSP_NO_RESPONSE or OCSP_INVALID. It returns OCSP_NO_RESPONSE if no response data is attached (514-516), and OCSP_INVALID if the OCSPResponse or the BasicOCSPResponse cannot be parsed, the response status is not zero, or the response type is not basic OCSP (521-553). It then goes through the response certificates, finds the signer with ocsp_find_signer, gets its public key, verifies the signature of the response data and verifies the signer certificate against the certificate store with the OCSP helper purpose; failures in this part go to fail with the result still OCSP_INVALID (556-655), except that an untrusted signer without the OCSP-signing extended key usage sets OCSP_NO_RESPONSE (658-698). It compares the issuer information across the SingleResponse values (a difference goes to fail with OCSP_INVALID) and remembers the one that matches the peer certificate's serial number and issuer (771-792). Without a matching single response it sets OCSP_NO_RESPONSE (801-805); a response outside its validity time goes to fail with OCSP_INVALID (808-812); certificate status 1 (revoked) sets OCSP_REVOKED, any other status except 0 sets OCSP_NO_RESPONSE, and status 0 sets OCSP_GOOD (815-830). All paths from the signature check on go through the fail label, which releases the allocated objects and returns result (831-839).
note: [R:n/a] still-rejected only for the wrong name; fixed under the real name check_ocsp_resp. Partly read: head (480-560), the key lines of the signer and verification part (580-700 by their goto and result lines) and the match and status part (770-831); the certificate-collecting code (556-610) and the middle details were not read line by line.

name: atheros_set_key
prose: Installs or deletes a key in the Atheros driver (driver_atheros.c:494-584; slice cut the head); it returns -1, -3, the result of atheros_del_key or the result of the SETKEY ioctl. The arguments come from the wpa_driver_set_key_params structure (alg, addr, key_idx, set_tx, key, key_len, 500-505). For WPA_ALG_NONE it returns atheros_del_key(drv, addr, key_idx) (507-508). Otherwise it maps the algorithm to an IEEE80211 cipher (WEP, TKIP, CCMP, BIP-CMAC-128, and with ATH_GCM_SUPPORT also CCMP-256, GCMP, GCMP-256, BIP-CMAC-256 and BIP-GMAC), returning -1 for any other algorithm (513-552), and returns -3 if key_len exceeds the key data field (554-557). It fills a ieee80211req_key: for a NULL or broadcast address it uses the broadcast address, the key index, and sets the default-key flag when set_tx; for a unicast address it uses that address with IEEE80211_KEYIX_NONE; it copies the key and calls set80211priv with IEEE80211_IOCTL_SETKEY, logs when the result is negative and returns that result (560-583).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: the prose precondition invents a params block, while the code takes alg/addr/key directly - wrong: atheros_set_key takes `struct wpa_driver_set_key_params *params` (494) and reads alg, addr, key_idx, set_tx, key and key_len from it (500-505). The real function starts at 494 (slice cut the head). Read in full; atheros_del_key and set80211priv not read.

name: wpa_driver_ndis_get_names
prose: Finds the NDIS network adapter that matches drv->ifname and stores its description (driver_ndis.c:2034-2307; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. There are two compile-time variants: with CONFIG_USE_NDISUIO (2036-2133) it queries NDISUIO bindings, and otherwise (2134-2305) it uses WinPcap's PacketGetAdapterNames. In the second variant it allocates an 8 KB buffer (returning -1 if that fails) and retries once with the length the call reports (2148-2160), splits the returned names and descriptions into arrays, and, when there are fewer descriptions than names, fills the missing ones with "stub description" (2242-2243); only if there are more descriptions than names (a count mismatch afterwards) does it free the buffer and return -1 (2245-2251). It looks for an adapter whose name contains the interface name, or whose description starts with it, and, when only the description matches, it rewrites drv->ifname with the adapter name (without the "\Device\NPF_" prefix) (2253-2274). No match returns -1 (2276-2281). Otherwise it copies the description, cut at the last " (" (2283-2297), into a new drv->adapter_desc and returns -1 if that allocation fails, else 0 (2299-2305). The names buffer is freed on those paths.
note: [R:right] reviewer: says a count mismatch returns -1, but the code fills stub descriptions when there are fewer descriptions than names - right (2242-2251). Partly read: the second variant's head and tail (2134-2160, 2232-2307); the parsing of the names and descriptions (2161-2231) and the NDISUIO variant (2036-2133) were scanned only by return lines.

name: nl80211_mgmt_subscribe_non_ap
prose: Registers the management frames a non-AP interface wants to receive from the nl80211 driver (driver_nl80211.c:2496-2679; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or -1. It allocates the management socket handle with nl80211_alloc_mgmt_handle and returns -1 if that fails (2502-2503). It registers authentication frames for ad-hoc mode, or for SAE when the driver has SAE but not SME (2507-2515), then registers one or more frame patterns with nl80211_register_frame or nl80211_register_action_frame for a long list of action frames (public action, WNM, fast transition, interworking, SA query, WPA/NAN/DPP vendor patterns, TDLS only when supported, RRM and others, 2519-2674). Each failed registration sets ret to -1 but registration continues; the NAN publication registration is retried without the multicast flag first (2570-2575). If the FT action registration (action category 6) succeeds and the driver does not report key management capabilities itself, it adds the FT key management flags to drv->capa (2608-2621). After all registrations it calls nl80211_mgmt_handle_register_eloop(bss) (2676), so the management socket is registered with eloop, and returns ret (2678).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: claims the function registers the mgmt socket with eloop, but it never calls nl80211_mgmt_handle_register_eloop - wrong: the call is at driver_nl80211.c:2676, just before `return ret`. Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: wpa_driver_nl80211_set_mode_impl
prose: Switches the interface to nl80211 mode nlmode (driver_nl80211.c:7353-7500; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and a nonzero value (-1 or the nl80211 error) on failure. It returns -1 on a forced test failure (7365-7366). It tries nl80211_set_mode; success, or a failure while the interface is already in nlmode, stores nlmode in drv->nlmode and goes to done (7368-7376); -ENODEV returns -1 (7378-7379); if nlmode equals the already stored mode the error is ignored and it goes to done with ret 0 (7381-7386). Otherwise, for up to 10 attempts, it brings the interface down (retrying after sleeps, leaving the loop on EACCES or ENODEV), optionally sets the frequency, removes an AP interface from its bridge, and retries nl80211_set_mode, delaying on -EBUSY, and keeps the last result as ret (7394-7441). A successful retry records the new mode and sets ignore_if_down_event (7443-7448); then it brings the interface up again, setting ret to -1 if that fails (7451-7456). At done a nonzero ret is returned with a log (7458-7462). Otherwise it disables or re-enables 11b rates for P2P interfaces, unsubscribes management frames, sets up the AP or tears it down when leaving AP mode (an AP setup failure returns -1), subscribes for mesh interfaces (failure returns -1), and, for a non-AP, non-mesh interface not in deinit, calls nl80211_mgmt_subscribe_non_ap, whose failure is only logged (7465-7498). It returns 0 at 7499.
note: [R:right] reviewer: returns 0 even if nl80211_mgmt_subscribe_non_ap fails, so subscriptions are not necessarily updated - right (7493-7497 only log "ignore for now"). Slice cut the head; function read in full; nl80211_set_mode and the helpers not read.

name: wpa_driver_roboswitch_leave
prose: Removes the multicast address addr for the given port mask from the Broadcom RoboSwitch address-resolution table (driver_roboswitch.c:286-354; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or -1. It converts the address to big-endian words and reads the ARL control configuration, returning -1 if that read fails or if bit 4 of it is clear (291-297). It reads the first address and vector entries, returning -1 if a read fails (299-303). If entry 1 matches both the address and the ports, it reads entry 2 (a read failure returns -1) and, when entry 2 also matches, clears bit 4 of the configuration and writes it back; when entry 2 does not match it reads entry 1 again (without checking the results of those reads) and writes it into slot 2 (305-333). If entry 1 does not match, it reads entry 2 (read failure returns -1) and, when it matches, writes it into slot 1, otherwise it returns -1 (334-351). The write calls and the re-reads inside the copy branch are not checked for errors, so those branches return 0 even if they fail. It returns 0 at 353.
note: [R:right] reviewer: claims any read failure returns -1, but the copy-branch re-reads are unchecked and still write/return 0 - right (321-326 ignore the results, and the writes at 317-332 and 345-350 are unchecked). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: wpa_driver_wext_event_link
prose: Handles a link add or remove event for the wext driver (driver_wext.c:534-577; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It zeroes an event structure and copies the interface name from buf into event.interface_status.ifname; if len is larger than the buffer it is reduced to the size minus one, but a len equal to the buffer size copies the whole buffer size, leaving the name without a terminating NUL (539-542). It sets the event to interface-removed (del) or interface-added and logs it (543-549). If the name equals the driver's own interface it ignores a removal when if_removed is already set and otherwise sets if_removed, and for an addition it ignores the event if the interface does not exist (if_nametoindex is 0) or if_removed is not set, and otherwise clears if_removed (551-574). It then delivers EVENT_INTERFACE_STATUS to the upper layer with wpa_supplicant_event (576).
note: [R:right] reviewer: it copies IFNAMSIZ bytes when len equals the buffer size, not at most IFNAMSIZ-1 - right (540-542 reduce len only when len is greater than the size). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: eap_sim_parse_attr
prose: Parses a list of EAP-SIM/AKA attributes between start and end into struct eap_sim_attrs (eap_sim_common.c:495-930; the packet name was a slice-level name, the slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It clears attr and sets id_req to NO_ID_REQ and notification, counter, selected_version and client_error_code to -1 (501-506). For each attribute it returns -1 if fewer than 2 bytes remain, if the attribute length (field times 4) runs past end, or if the length field is zero (508-524). It then switches on the attribute type; for each known type it checks the attribute length against what that type needs (RAND, AUTN, PADDING, NONCE_MT, MAC, NOTIFICATION, IDENTITY, VERSION_LIST, SELECTED_VERSION, COUNTER, COUNTER_TOO_SMALL, NONCE_S, CLIENT_ERROR_CODE, IV, ENCR_DATA, NEXT_PSEUDONYM and the AKA ones, with AT_KDF and AT_BIDDING requiring exactly 2 bytes of data), returning -1 on a wrong length, and stores pointers to or copies of the data in attr (530-908). AT_PERMANENT_ID_REQ, AT_ANY_ID_REQ and AT_FULLAUTH_ID_REQ only set attr->id_req and do not check their payload length (590-593, 614-617, 666-669). An unknown attribute with a type below 128 returns -1; one at or above 128 is skipped (910-920). It advances by the attribute length and returns 0 when all attributes are consumed (923-929).
note: [R:right] reviewer: AT_PERMANENT_ID_REQ, AT_ANY_ID_REQ and AT_FULLAUTH_ID_REQ accept a nonzero payload; the prose said wrong-length known attributes return -1 - right for those three (590-593, 614-617, 666-669 do not look at alen). Partly read: head (495-531), the three ID_REQ cases, the AT_KDF, AT_BIDDING and default cases and the tail (880-930), plus a scan of all return -1 lines; the other attribute cases (531-880) were not read line by line.

name: eap_aka_process_challenge
prose: Processes an EAP-AKA or AKA' Challenge request on the peer (eap_aka.c:1052-1235; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer built by one of the helper functions, or NULL. It first verifies AT_CHECKCODE if present, returning a client error (UNABLE_TO_PROCESS_PACKET) on a mismatch (1065-1075). For AKA' it requires a non-empty AT_KDF_INPUT, stores the network name (failure or missing input returns an authentication reject) and, after the KDF negotiation and KDF-count checks, may return the KDF negotiation response (1080-1109). It then checks the other attributes, runs the USIM/UMTS authentication (a failure returns an authentication reject or a synchronization-failure response, and a NULL result is returned in the case at 1152), and verifies the MAC (a failure returns a client error) (1110-1196). For AKA' it derives the CK' and IK' and the keys including K_re, MSK and EMSK with eap_aka_prime_derive_keys (1168-1182); for plain AKA it derives the master key with eap_aka_derive_mk and the keys with eap_sim_derive_keys, which does not derive K_re (1184-1186). It then handles the result indication and the next-pseudonym and reauthentication identity attributes, moves the state to success or result-indication wait unless the state is FAILURE, and returns eap_aka_response_challenge(data, id) (1201-1234).
note: [R:right] reviewer: on the AKA path it does not derive K_re; only AKA' derives K_re - right (1180-1182 versus 1184-1186). Partly read: head (1052-1100), the key-derivation part (1160-1234) and the return lines; the middle (1110-1160, 1196-1230) was scanned only by its return statements.

name: eap_aka_umts_auth
prose: Runs the UMTS authentication for the EAP-AKA peer (eap_aka.c:282-378; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success, -1 on error, or a value from the helper it delegates to (for example a negative resynchronisation code from the card or simulator). It returns -1 if the peer configuration is not available (288-290). With an external SIM it returns the result of eap_aka_ext_sim_result when a response is already stored in the configuration, and otherwise the result of eap_aka_ext_sim_req (292-297). With PC/SC it returns the result of scard_umts_auth, which fills res, ik, ck and auts (299-303). With CONFIG_USIM_SIMULATOR and a password it parses "K:OPc:SQN" from the password (a password shorter than 78 characters, bad hex or a missing ':' returns -1) and returns the result of milenage_check (305-337). With CONFIG_USIM_HARDCODED it fills fixed test values, returns -1 if AUTN is not the expected test value, and returns 0 (340-369); otherwise, with neither compiled in, it logs and returns -1 (371-376).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the precondition requires a configuration, but the code handles conf == NULL and returns -1 - right (288-290). Slice cut the head; function read in full; scard_umts_auth, milenage_check and the external-SIM helpers not read.

name: eap_fast_process_decrypted
prose: Processes the decrypted Phase 2 TLVs of an EAP-FAST message on the peer (eap_fast.c:1187-1297; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or the result of eap_fast_encrypt_response, and puts the encrypted answer in *out_data. If the TLVs cannot be parsed it returns 0 without setting *out_data (1198-1199). If parsing produced a response it encrypts and returns it (1200-1202); a failure result TLV or intermediate failure result TLV gets a matching failure TLV as the response (1204-1214). Otherwise it handles the crypto-binding TLV (failure sets failed), an intermediate success result, an EAP payload TLV and a PAC TLV (a PAC with a result that is not success only sets failed), requests a tunnel PAC when authenticated provisioning needs one, prepends a final result TLV and, when the tunnel result was success, there was no failure, a crypto binding was present and phase 2 succeeded, updates the method state and decision: anonymous provisioning ends as DONE with DECISION_FAIL and expected_failure, otherwise MAY_CONT (provisioning) or DONE with DECISION_UNCOND_SUCC (1216-1287). An empty response is replaced by a one-byte buffer (1289-1293), and the function returns the result of eap_fast_encrypt_response (1295). The method state is not updated to success on paths with failed set or without a crypto-binding result.
note: [R:right] reviewer: claims it always assembles a response and sets success even when resp is NULL or failed, but the code can return without out_data - right (1198-1199 return 0 before any response; success is set only under the condition at 1270-1272). Slice cut the head; function read in full; the TLV processing helpers not read.

name: eap_fast_process
prose: Processes one EAP-FAST request on the peer (eap_fast.c:1537-1677; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. It calls eap_peer_tls_process_init and returns NULL if that gives nothing (1550-1553). For a Start message it handles it with eap_fast_process_start (failure returns NULL) and clears the A-ID length (1558-1563). If the TLS connection is already established and not resuming it decrypts the message and builds the Phase 2 response with eap_fast_decrypt, which returns a result in res and a response in resp; a negative result sets METHOD_DONE with DECISION_FAIL (1568-1580). Otherwise it handles a pending external certificate check (good returns the stored pending response, bad ends with DECISION_FAIL, still waiting returns NULL) (1582-1608), runs the TLS handshake with eap_peer_tls_process_helper (negative result: METHOD_DONE with DECISION_FAIL and the response it produced is returned), stores the response and returns NULL while an external check is pending (1611-1629), and when the TLS connection became established decides on anonymous provisioning and derives keys (a failure frees the response and returns NULL) (1631-1656). If res is 2 the pending Phase 2 request is stored and decrypted (1659-1667). If res is 1 it frees resp and returns a TLS ACK (1670-1673); otherwise it returns resp (1676). Application data that has been consumed does not by itself make the function return NULL: it continues through eap_fast_decrypt and returns its response.
note: [R:right] reviewer: claims NULL when application data is consumed, but the code continues to eap_fast_decrypt and returns its resp - right (1568-1571 and 1676). Slice cut the head; function read in full except the logging lines; the TLS helpers not read.

name: eap_fast_load_pac_bin
prose: Loads PAC entries in the binary format from a file or config blob into a list (eap_fast_pac.c:748-861; the packet name eap_fast_read_pac_bin does not exist). It returns -1 if pac_file is NULL (758-759). A name starting with "blob://" is looked up as a configuration blob and any other name is read as a file; a missing blob or an unreadable file returns 0 (no PAC entries) (761-779). An empty input returns 0 (781-785); a header shorter than 6 bytes, or with a wrong magic or format version, returns -1 (787-794). It then parses entries: for each it needs enough bytes for the type, the key, and the lengths (otherwise goes to parse_fail), allocates an entry, copies the opaque and info parts with bounds checks, derives the A-ID and appends the entry to the list (799-843). At the end it frees the file buffer (not a blob) and returns 0 (845-851). parse_fail frees the file buffer and the entry being built and returns -1, while entries already appended to *pac_root before the failure are kept (853-860).
note: [R:n/a] previously dropped as a wrong name; the function exists (eap_fast_load_pac_bin, eap_fast_pac.c:748-861) and is fixed. Read in full.

name: eap_ikev2_process
prose: Processes one EAP-IKEv2 request on the peer (eap_ikev2.c:328-435; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. It validates the EAP header; failure sets ret->ignore and returns NULL (339-343). It reads the flags (none for an empty fragment ack), checks the integrity (ICV), and the optional length field; failures set ret->ignore and return NULL (350-378). In the state WAIT_FRAG_ACK a non-empty message sets ignore and returns NULL, and an empty one moves to PROC_MSG and returns eap_ikev2_build_msg (383-392). A continuation fragment is appended with eap_ikev2_process_cont (failure sets ignore and returns NULL) (395-398), and a message with the more-fragments flag returns eap_ikev2_process_fragment (400-404). Otherwise it uses a stack buffer for an unfragmented message, runs ikev2_responder_process (on failure it sets the state to FAIL and returns NULL), and frees the input buffer only if it is not that stack buffer (406-421). If no output exists it builds it with ikev2_responder_build (NULL returns NULL) and moves to PROC_MSG, returning eap_ikev2_build_msg (423-434).

name: eap_peap_decrypt
prose: Decrypts and processes one PEAP Phase 2 message on the peer (eap_peap.c:792-1018; slice cut the head); it returns 0 when the message was handled (a response, if any, is in *out_data), 1 when only a TLS acknowledgement is needed or there is nothing to process, and otherwise the nonzero result of the TLS helper. If an earlier Phase 2 request is pending it uses that instead of decrypting and jumps to continue_req (807-816). An empty input returns 1 with METHOD_DONE and DECISION_COND_SUCC only when sm->workaround is set and phase 2 has already succeeded (818-829); an empty input otherwise returns the result of eap_peer_tls_encrypt of an empty message (830-835). It decrypts with eap_peer_tls_decrypt and returns its result if that is nonzero (837-839); an empty decrypted message is freed and gives 1 (840-843). At continue_req it examines the inner EAP header and handles Request, Success, Failure and other codes (908-1000): on the paths shown it can return 0 early for malformed or ignored inner messages (868, 887, 896, 915, 932) or 1 (944). A response built for the inner message is encrypted with eap_peer_tls_encrypt, skipping the header strip for a TLV response and, for PEAP version 0, stripping the EAP header otherwise (995-1010), and freed; the function returns 0 (1017).

Partly read: head (792-850) and the response encryption tail (995-1018); the inner EAP request/success/failure handling (850-995) was scanned only by its return lines.

name: eap_pwd_perform_confirm_exchange
prose: Verifies the server's Confirm message of EAP-pwd and builds the peer's Confirm (eap_pwd.c:690-881; the packet name eap_pwd_build_confirm does not exist, and the slice cut the head); it returns nothing and reports through data->outbuf, data->state and ret. It uses a single exit, fin. If data->state is not PWD_Confirm_Req it sets ret->ignore and goes to fin; a payload that is not 32 bytes long also goes to fin (701-711). Otherwise it computes the expected server confirm value as a SHA-256 hash over k, the server element, the server scalar, the peer element, the peer scalar and the cipher suite, compares it with the payload in constant time and goes to fin on a mismatch (713-796); allocation, hash or conversion failures also go to fin. It then computes its own confirm value (the same elements in the peer order), derives the MSK, EMSK and session id with compute_keys, allocates data->outbuf of 32 bytes and fills it (805-866). At fin it clears and frees the scratch buffer; if data->outbuf is NULL it sets METHOD_DONE, DECISION_FAIL and the FAILURE state, otherwise it sets the state SUCCESS_ON_FRAG_COMPLETION; a hash context left open is finalised (868-880). So a wrong state or length also ends in the FAILURE state, with ret->ignore set only for the wrong state.
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: a state mismatch returns early, not via the common exit, so cleanup and the state update are not run - wrong: the mismatch does `ret->ignore = true; goto fin;` (701-704), so the cleanup and the failure state update at 868-876 do run. The real function is eap_pwd_perform_confirm_exchange; read in full; the crypto helpers not read.

name: eap_sake_process_identity
prose: Handles an EAP-SAKE Identity request on the peer (eap_sake.c:140-180; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. If the state is not IDENTITY it sets ret->ignore to true and returns NULL (150-153). It parses the attributes (failure returns NULL without touching ret->ignore), requires AT_PERM_ID_REQ or AT_ANY_ID_REQ (otherwise returns NULL) (157-164), builds an Identity response with the peer id attribute and moves the state to CHALLENGE (168-177), returning NULL if the response buffer cannot be allocated (170-171).

name: eap_sake_process_confirm
prose: Handles an EAP-SAKE Confirm request on the peer (eap_sake.c:285-367; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. If the state is not CONFIRM it sets ret->ignore to true and returns NULL (298-301). It parses the attributes and returns NULL if parsing fails or AT_MIC_S is missing (305-312). It computes the expected server MIC; if the computation fails or the MIC differs it sets the state to FAILURE, METHOD_DONE, DECISION_FAIL and no notifications and returns an Auth-Reject message (314-337). Otherwise it builds a Confirm response with AT_MIC_P and computes the peer MIC over it (a computation failure frees the response and returns NULL), then sets the state to SUCCESS, METHOD_DONE, DECISION_UNCOND_SUCC and no notifications, and returns the response (342-366).

name: eap_sake_process
prose: Processes one EAP-SAKE request on the peer (eap_sake.c:370-437; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. It validates the EAP header and the SAKE header; a failure sets ret->ignore and returns NULL (381-385). A session id different from the stored one sets ignore and returns NULL; otherwise the session id is stored (399-406). It then sets ret->ignore to false, methodState to METHOD_MAY_CONT, decision to DECISION_FAIL and allowNotifications to true (408-411) before dispatching on the subtype: Identity, Challenge or Confirm go to their handlers (which may set ignore themselves, for example when the state is wrong), and any other subtype sets ignore and returns NULL (413-431). If the method state is METHOD_DONE afterwards it clears allowNotifications, and it returns the handler's response (433-436); a NULL response from a handler therefore does not by itself imply that ret->ignore is false.

name: eap_peer_sake_register
prose: Registers the EAP-SAKE peer method (eap_sake.c:503-521; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It allocates an eap_method structure for the IETF vendor, type SAKE and the name "SAKE" and returns -1 if that fails (507-510). It sets the init, deinit, process, isKeyAvailable, getKey, getSessionId and get_emsk callbacks (512-518) and returns the result of eap_peer_method_register(eap) (520), so a registration failure is returned by that call (the allocation is not freed in this function).

name: eap_teap_phase2_request
prose: Handles a Phase 2 EAP request inside the EAP-TEAP tunnel on the peer (eap_teap.c:404-498; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or -1 and the response in *resp. It returns -1 if the request is no longer than the EAP header or, for the expanded type, shorter than the expanded header (418-432). For an Identity request it drops the inner EAP method, builds an identity response with eap_sm_buildIdentity and returns 0 (438-442). If the requested method differs from the running one it deinitialises the inner method; when no inner method is chosen it selects one, and if that fails it builds a Nak response and returns -1 if the Nak fails, else 0 (444-457). If the inner method cannot be initialised it sets METHOD_DONE with DECISION_FAIL and returns -1 (459-467). It runs the inner method's process function on the request and records whether the inner method is done (469-474); with no response or an inner failure it sets the outer state to METHOD_MAY_CONT with DECISION_FAIL, and an inner success sets phase2_success (475-486). With no response and a pending identity, password, OTP, new-password or SIM request in the configuration it stores a copy of the request in pending_phase2_req (a failed copy leaves it NULL, unchecked) and returns 0 (488-493); with no response and nothing pending it returns -1 (494-495); otherwise it returns 0 (497).

name: eap_teap_load_pac_bin
prose: Loads PAC entries in the binary format from a file or config blob into a list (eap_teap_pac.c:752-868; the packet name eap_teap_read_pac_bin does not exist). It returns -1 if pac_file is NULL (762-763). A name starting with "blob://" is looked up as a configuration blob and any other name is read as a file; a missing blob or unreadable file returns 0, meaning no PAC entries (765-783). An empty input returns 0 (785-789); a header shorter than 6 bytes or with the wrong magic or format version returns -1 (791-798). It then parses the entries: each needs enough bytes for type, key and the two length fields, allocates an entry, copies the opaque and info parts after bounds checks, derives the A-ID and appends the entry to the list; any shortage or allocation failure goes to parse_fail (803-846). On success it frees the file buffer (not a blob) and returns 0; parse_fail frees the buffer and the entry being built and returns -1, keeping entries already appended to the list.

name: eap_wsc_build_msg
prose: Builds the next EAP-WSC response fragment from the pending output buffer (eap_wsc.c:310-374; slice cut the head); it returns the response or NULL. It sets ret->ignore to false and allowNotifications to true (317-319). It chooses how much of the remaining output to send: when 2 plus the remaining data exceeds the fragment size it sends fragment_size - 2 bytes with the more-fragments flag and, on the first fragment, adds the length flag and an extra 2 bytes for the total length (321-333). It allocates the EAP message and returns NULL if that fails, before ret->methodState and ret->decision are set (334-337); this failure leaves those two fields as they were. Otherwise it writes the opcode, flags, the length (first fragment) and the data, advances out_used, and sets methodState to METHOD_MAY_CONT and the decision to DECISION_FAIL (339-349). If the whole buffer has been sent it frees it and moves to FAIL (with METHOD_DONE) after an ACK in failure state, a NACK or a Done, and to MESG otherwise; if more remains it moves to WAIT_FRAG_ACK (351-371). It returns the response (373).

name: eap_sm_Policy_update
prose: Applies a peer's Nak method list to the user's configured methods (eap_server.c:1673-1687; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns without effect if nak_list, sm or sm->user is NULL (1676-1677). If the user entry is a phase 2 entry it sets sm->decision to DECISION_FAILURE and returns (1679-1683). Otherwise it calls eap_sm_process_nak(sm, nak_list, len), which reads sm->user_eap_method_index and the user's method table and removes from that table, by shifting later entries down and ending with an empty entry, every method that the peer's list does not support (eap_server.c:1619-1670), so the table of sm->user is modified there.

Slice cut the head; function read in full, plus eap_sm_process_nak.

name: eap_sm_Policy_getDecision
prose: Decides what the EAP server should do next (eap_server.c:1722-1801; slice cut the head); it returns a DECISION_* value. With a pass-through configuration (no local EAP server), an identity and no reauthentication start it returns DECISION_PASSTHROUGH (1724-1727). If the current method (not Identity) reports success it sets update_user to true and returns DECISION_SUCCESS (1729-1735); a finished method that is not successful sets update_user and returns DECISION_FAILURE (1737-1743). If there is no user or update_user is set, an identity exists and no reauthentication starts, it looks up the user with eap_user_get: a failed lookup returns DECISION_FAILURE without changing update_user or start_reauth, and an identity request loop sets update_user and returns DECISION_FAILURE; otherwise it clears update_user (1745-1772). It then clears start_reauth (1773), returns DECISION_CONTINUE if the user still has a method at the current index (1775-1783), DECISION_INITIATE_REAUTH_START when an ERP start should be sent (1785-1790), DECISION_CONTINUE when no identity or id is known yet (1792-1796) and DECISION_FAILURE otherwise (1800).

name: SM_STATE(EAP, INITIATE_RECEIVED)
prose: Generated state function for the EAP server state INITIATE_RECEIVED, which processes an EAP-Initiate/Re-auth message (macro invocation SM_STATE(EAP, INITIATE_RECEIVED) at eap_server.c:797-992); it returns nothing. It enters the state, clears rxInitiate, and validates the ERP header, requiring at least 4 bytes; failures go to fail, which sets sm->ignore to true (812-830, 990-991). It parses the flags, the sequence number and the TLVs, and requires a keyName-NAI of at most 253 bytes (833-862). Without a local EAP server it stores the keyName-NAI as the identity for backend authentication and returns, or goes to fail if the copy fails (864-880). With a local server it looks up the ERP key for the NAI; with no key it jumps to report_error, which calls erp_send_finish_reauth with a NULL key and the default failure flag, and that function still builds a Finish/Re-auth message (without authentication tag) in that case (882-887, 986-987, and 703-735). A replayed sequence number, too little room for the tag, a cryptosuite mismatch, a tag mismatch, no matching cryptosuite or bad TLVs go to fail (889-979). On success it stores the sequence number, clears the failure bit in the response flags and sends the Finish/Re-auth with erp_send_finish_reauth (983-987).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: with no ERP key, erp_send_finish_reauth is called with NULL, which sets eapFail and returns, so no Finish/Re-auth is sent - wrong: erp_send_finish_reauth treats a NULL key as hash_len 0 and goes on to allocate and build the message (eap_server.c:713-735); nothing in the lines read sets eapFail. The packet name "EAP INITIATE_RECEIVED" is the macro SM_STATE(EAP, INITIATE_RECEIVED). Partly read: 797-990 line by line; the tail of erp_send_finish_reauth (736-794) was not read.

name: eap_aka_check_identity
prose: Examines the identity received by the EAP-AKA server and, if it is recognised, skips the identity exchange (eap_server_aka.c:155-218; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and changes the state through helpers. It takes the identity from sm->sim_aka_permanent when that is set, otherwise from sm->identity, and extracts the user name with sim_get_username, returning if that gives NULL (159-171). If eap_aka_check_identity_reauth recognises the user name as a fast re-authentication name (result above 0) it frees the name and returns (173-180); a recognised name whose re-authentication cannot be used is handled inside that helper, whose effects (for example on data->reauth) I did not read. If a permanent identity was supplied in the IDENTITY state it copies it into data->permanent and starts the full authentication (182-189). If the user name has the pseudonym prefix of the method it looks up the permanent identity: when none is found it frees the name and returns so that the permanent identity will be requested, otherwise it copies it and starts the full authentication (192-214). The user name is freed at the end (217).

prose: Builds the next EAP-AKA request of the server according to its state (eap_server_aka.c:684-704; slice cut the head). It clears data->auts_reported (688) and switches on data->state: IDENTITY returns eap_aka_build_identity, CHALLENGE eap_aka_build_challenge, REAUTH eap_aka_build_reauth and NOTIFICATION eap_aka_build_notification, each returning the buffer the helper builds (689-697). Any other state logs an unexpected state and falls out of the switch, returning NULL (698-703).

name: eap_server_psk_register
prose: Registers the EAP-PSK server method (eap_server_psk.c:506-527; the packet name eap_psk_method_register does not exist); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It allocates an eap_method structure with eap_server_method_alloc for the IETF vendor, type PSK, and returns -1 if that fails (510-513). It sets the init, reset, buildReq, check, process, isDone, getKey, isSuccess, get_emsk and getSessionId callbacks (515-524) and returns the result of eap_server_method_register(eap) (526); the allocated structure is not freed in this function if registration fails.

name: eap_teap_process_phase2_response
prose: Processes the peer's Phase 2 EAP response inside the TEAP tunnel on the server (eap_server_teap.c:1069-1214; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and starts the next inner method through eap_teap_phase2_init. It returns at once if the inner method is not initialised (1083-1087). A Nak response from the peer: with EAP_SERVER_TNC and the current inner method being TNC (a required TNC negotiation) it requests a failure and starts that, without calling eap_sm_process_nak and returns (1099-1107); otherwise it calls eap_sm_process_nak and starts the next configured method, or a failure request if none remains, then returns (1109-1124). Otherwise it calls the inner method's check, which on a rejection requests a failure with TEAP_ERROR_INNER_METHOD and returns (1129-1134), and then its process; if the method is not done it returns, and if it is done but not successful it starts a failure request (1136-1147). On success it acts on the TEAP state: in PHASE2_ID it checks the identity type and the user database (failure requests an error), then chooses the first configured method (or EAP-pwd for anonymous provisioning) and moves to PHASE2_METHOD; in PHASE2_METHOD or CRYPTO_BINDING it updates the ICMK, moves to CRYPTO_BINDING, increments the EAP sequence and may start TNC; in FAILURE it does nothing; other states are logged (1149-1211). Finally it initialises the chosen next method (1213).
note: [R:right] reviewer: a NAK on a required TNC bypasses eap_sm_process_nak, contrary to the prose - right (1099-1107 return before 1109). Slice cut the head; function read in full; eap_teap_phase2_init and eap_sm_process_nak (read in another record) not re-read.

name: eap_tnc_process
prose: Processes a received EAP-TNC response on the server (eap_server_tnc.c:446-537; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and works through data->state. It returns at once, with no state change, if the EAP header is not valid, or if the message is a 1-byte ack while the state is DONE or FAIL (456-466). It reads the flags and the optional length field: a length field that is truncated, smaller than the data present or above 75000 sets the state to FAIL and returns (474-491). In the WAIT_FRAG_ACK state, more than a 1-byte message sets FAIL and returns, and otherwise the state becomes CONTINUE (495-505). A continuation fragment that cannot be appended sets FAIL (507-510); a message with the more-fragments flag is processed as a fragment and sets FAIL on error or FRAG_ACK on success, then returns (512-518); a message after FRAG_ACK sets the state CONTINUE (519-522). Otherwise it uses the received data as the input buffer (a stack buffer when there was no earlier fragment), calls tncs_process on it, and frees the input buffer unless it is the stack buffer (524-536).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: an invalid EAP header sets the state to FAIL, not ignored with the state unchanged - wrong: an invalid header returns at eap_server_tnc.c:456-458 before any state is touched; FAIL is set only for bad length fields, wrong fragments and processing errors (477, 488, 499, 508, 515). Slice cut the head; function read in full; tncs_process and the fragment helpers not read.

name: eap_ttls_buildReq
prose: Builds the next EAP-TTLS request of the server (eap_server_ttls.c:466-510; slice cut the head). If the TLS fragment state is FRAG_ACK it returns a TLS ACK message (470-473); if it is WAIT_FRAG_ACK it returns the next TLS fragment (475-478). Otherwise it switches on the TTLS state: START returns eap_ttls_build_start; PHASE1 changes the state to PHASE2_START when the TLS connection is established and then breaks out of the switch; PHASE2_METHOD and PHASE2_MSCHAPV2_RESP replace the pending TLS output buffer with the encapsulated inner EAP request or the MS-CHAPv2 response and break; any other state logs and returns NULL (480-505). After a break it returns eap_server_tls_build_msg for the TLS output, so in PHASE1 the TLS message is returned after the possible state transition as well (508-509).

name: SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, DISCONNECTED)
prose: Generated state function for the AUTH_PAE state DISCONNECTED (macro invocation SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, DISCONNECTED) at eapol_auth_sm.c:217-246); it returns nothing. Before entering the state it records whether it came from INITIALIZE, whether it is a pre-authentication logoff from ABORTING (a logoff while not authenticated) and the logoff flag, and counts an EAPOL-Logoff received in the CONNECTING or AUTHENTICATED states in the matching counter (219-229). Unless it came from INITIALIZE or it is a pre-authentication logoff, it calls the finished callback of the EAPOL layer with the logoff flag and sets sm->stopped to true if the callback returns nonzero (237-245).

prose: Generated state function for the AUTH_PAE state RESTART (macro invocation SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, RESTART) at eapol_auth_sm.c:249-263); it returns nothing. When the previous state is AUTHENTICATED it increments the counters for re-authentications, EAPOL-Start and EAPOL-Logoff events that are pending (251-258).
